observations.name: op-supernode v1.0.4
observations.title: op-supernode v1.0.4
observations.body:
## Overview

> [!IMPORTANT]
> This is a recommended release for op-supernode operators. It contains two fixes to how the safe head is tracked after an L1 reorg on chains with interop enabled.

## Other changes

### Safe head

- After an L1 reorg moves a chain's local-safe head below its last cross-verified block, the `safe` tag reported to the execution client and in `optimism_syncStatus` now holds at the last verified block instead of advancing onto blocks that have not been cross-verified. It also holds after a resync until local-safe catches up with the verified head. The `op_node_supernode_super_authority_reorg_signals_total` metric gains a `reason="ahead_of_local_safe"` label value for this case (#22982)
- With `--safedb.path` set, a derivation reset now truncates the safe head database to the local-safe head rather than the cross-safe head. Previously, whenever cross-safe lagged local-safe at reset, the entries in between were deleted and never re-recorded, leaving a gap that made `superroot_atTimestamp` and `optimism_safeHeadAtL1Block` answer with a later L1 block than the correct one, without any error. New gaps no longer form, but an existing gap is not repaired: rebuild the safe head database to clear it (#22997)

### Metrics

- Virtual nodes now record `op_node_supernode_unsafe_payload_arrival_delay_seconds`, the delay between a block's timestamp and its arrival over p2p (#22967)

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/compare/op-supernode/v1.0.3...op-supernode/v1.0.4

**🚢 Docker Image:**

- https://us-docker.pkg.dev/oplabs-tools-artifacts/images/op-supernode:v1.0.4

observations.name: op-reth v2.6.0
observations.title: op-reth v2.6.0
observations.body:
## Overview

> [!IMPORTANT]
> This is a recommended release for all op-reth operators. It contains the update to reth v2.5.2, which removes two engine flags and changes the engine's persistence defaults, and a transaction pool fix for senders whose later transactions cannot cover their L1 data and operator fees.

## Breaking changes

- **`--engine.sparse-trie-max-hot-slots` and `--engine.sparse-trie-max-hot-accounts` removed** (#22495). The node refuses to start if either flag, or the `--engine.sparse-trie-max-storage-tries` alias, is passed. Remove them from launch configuration before upgrading.
- **Engine persistence defaults changed** (#22495). `--engine.persistence-threshold` now defaults to 7 instead of 2, and `--engine.memory-block-buffer-target` no longer has a fixed default: its effective value is the smaller of the persistence threshold and 5, so a node on default settings now keeps 5 blocks in memory ahead of the last persisted block instead of 0. Pass `--engine.persistence-threshold 2 --engine.memory-block-buffer-target 0` to keep the previous behaviour.
- **`testing_buildBlockV1` no longer skips invalid transactions by default** (#22495). Callers that rely on the old behaviour must start the node with `--testing.skip-invalid-transactions`.
- **`eth_getMultiProof` is not served** (#22495). Upstream reth now installs this method by default; op-reth removes it from every RPC transport, including the authenticated endpoint. We may reinstate it later if needed.
- **`isSystemTx` is now a JSON boolean** (#22946). Transaction RPC responses for deposits with the system-transaction flag set return `"isSystemTx": true` instead of `"0x1"`, matching op-geth. Only deposits in pre-Regolith blocks carry the flag, and no chain in the superchain registry has such blocks. On a chain that does, RPC consumers must accept the boolean form, and kona-node must be upgraded to v1.7.2 alongside, since it no longer decodes the hex form.

## Other changes

### Upstream

- Update reth to v2.5.2, with a backport of the upstream fix that keeps the Engine API responsive while persisted state is handed off during a payload build (paradigmxyz/reth#26708). Among the upstream changes: pending payload builds are finalized when resolved early, storage wipes of destroyed accounts are handled correctly in batched persistence, ExEx write-ahead log recovery tolerates non-contiguous file IDs, the discovery fork filter updates at fork activation without a restart, and `--trusted-peers` and `--bootnodes` accept ENRs. New flags `--engine.txpool-prewarming`, `--engine.sender-recovery-cache` and `--dev.finality-depth` are available. `debug_executionWitness` accepts a block hash as well as a number, and `debug_executePayload` returns the ancestor headers it used. revm moves to 42 and alloy to 2.3 (#22495)

### Transaction pool

- A sender's transaction cost now includes the L1 data fee and operator fee reserved at admission, not only the L2 execution cost. Later-nonce transactions that cannot cover the fees of the sender's earlier ones are classified as queued instead of pending, as op-geth does, so the block builder no longer retries them every block and they expire after the pool's transaction lifetime. Single-transaction admission is unchanged (#23076, #23077)

### Metrics

- New SDM metrics are exported on every node: the gauges `reth_op_sdm_operator_opt_in` (the current value, which follows `admin_setOperatorSdmOptIn`) and `reth_op_sdm_operator_opt_in_configured` (the `--rollup.operator-sdm-opt-in` value at boot), which differ when a restart would change the opt-in; and the counters `reth_op_sdm_block_gas_total`, `reth_op_sdm_refund_entries_total` and `reth_op_sdm_refund_gas_total`, recorded for every imported block. The refund counters stay at zero on chains without SDM (#22927, #22961, #22931)

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/compare/op-reth/v2.5.0...op-reth/v2.6.0

**🚢 Docker Image:**

- https://us-docker.pkg.dev/oplabs-tools-artifacts/images/op-reth:v2.6.0

observations.name: op-node v1.19.9
observations.title: op-node v1.19.9
observations.body:
## Overview

> [!IMPORTANT]
> This is a recommended release for sequencer operators, and an optional one for other node operators. It contains a change to how sequencers publish new blocks, which removes the block-building stalls caused by slow remote signers, and the removal of the server-side RPC metrics.

## Other changes

### Sequencer

- Sequencers now insert each new block into their own execution client before publishing it, and publishing runs in the background instead of holding up the next block. A slow remote signer (`--signer.endpoint`) no longer delays block production, and peers only receive blocks the sequencer has already adopted as its head, so a block the execution client rejects can no longer cause a reorg on every verifier. Failed publishes are retried about once a second until the block leaves the gossip window set by `--p2p.gossip.timestamp.threshold`, after which it is dropped with a `Giving up on publishing block` error log. `publishing_errors_total` now counts every failed attempt rather than one per block. New metrics: `sequencer_insert_seconds`, `sequencer_publish_handoff_seconds`, `publish_queue_len`, `publish_delay_seconds`, `dropped_publishes_total`, and `unsafe_payload_arrival_delay_seconds`, which every node records when it receives a block over p2p (#22967)

### Metrics

- The server-side RPC metrics `op_node_default_rpc_server_*` (requests, durations, responses, parameter and result sizes, notifications sent) and `op_node_default_rpc_client_notifications_received_total` are no longer exported. Dashboards and alerts that query them need updating; the `op_node_default_rpc_client_*` request metrics are unchanged (#23114, #23055)

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/compare/op-node/v1.19.8...op-node/v1.19.9

**🚢 Docker Image:**

- https://us-docker.pkg.dev/oplabs-tools-artifacts/images/op-node:v1.19.9

observations.name: op-deployer/v0.8.0
observations.title: op-deployer/v0.8.0
observations.body:
## Overview

> [!IMPORTANT]
> This is the op-deployer release for [op-contracts/v8.0.0](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/releases/tag/op-contracts%2Fv8.0.0) ([Upgrade 20](https://gov.optimism.io/t/upgrade-20-super-root-dispute-games-opcm-v8-0-0/10856)). Use it to deploy new chains with op-contracts/v8.0.0. It contains a new staged `prepare` / `prestate` / `continue` deployment workflow, Super Root dispute games for new chains, Karst at genesis by default, more reliable gas estimation, and several breaking command and flag removals.

## Breaking changes

- **`upgrade` command removed** (#21945). `op-deployer upgrade` and all its version subcommands (`v2.0.0` through `v6.0.0-rc.2`, and `embedded`) are gone, and op-deployer no longer upgrades existing chains from any earlier op-contracts release.
- **`manage migrate` command removed** (#21929). The super-root migration command and its flags (`--starting-respected-game-type`, `--dispute-game-type`, `--dispute-game-enabled` and others) are gone, with no replacement in op-deployer.
- **Contract verification is on by default; `--verify` removed** (#21947). `apply`, `bootstrap superchain` and `bootstrap implementations` now verify contracts unless `--no-verify` (`DEPLOYER_NO_VERIFY`) is set. Remove `--verify` / `DEPLOYER_VERIFY` from scripts — op-deployer rejects it as unknown. The `--verifier` default changes from `etherscan` to `etherscan,blockscout`, and a verification failure is now logged with a retry command instead of failing a successful deployment.
- **`apply --validate` and `op-validator` removed** (#21308). Remove `--validate` / `DEPLOYER_VALIDATE` and run `op-deployer validate auto` after `apply` instead.
- **`--op-program-svc-url` removed** (#21299). Remove `--op-program-svc-url` / `DEPLOYER_OP_PROGRAM_SVC_URL`. op-deployer no longer fetches prestates from an op-program service, and `state.json` no longer carries `prestateManifest`; existing state files still load. For permissionless games, record the prestate with the new `prestate` command.
- **New chains deploy Super Root dispute games** (#21689, #22128, #21720). The default `respectedGameType` changes from `1` (`PERMISSIONED_CANNON`) to `5` (`SUPER_PERMISSIONED`). An intent that sets `respectedGameType = 1` now fails with `DeployOPChain: dispute game type does not match OPCM super root mode`; remove the override or set it to `5`. A new permissionless chain can start on `SUPER_CANNON_KONA` (`9`) through the `prepare` workflow, with `SUPER_PERMISSIONED` registered as its fallback.
- **`manage add-game-type-v2` config for Super Root games** (#20641, #20363). Game type `5` (`SUPER_PERMISSIONED`) now takes `superPermissionedDisputeGameConfig: {proposer}` instead of `permissionedDisputeGameConfig`, and game type `4` (`SUPER_CANNON`) is rejected.
- **Interop hardfork renamed to Lagoon** (#21105, #21370). The intent override `l2GenesisInteropTimeOffset` is now `l2GenesisLagoonTimeOffset`; the old key is silently ignored, so rename it in any intent that schedules the fork. The generated rollup config key `interop_time` becomes `lagoon_time`, and the L2 genesis key `interopTime` becomes `lagoonTime`.

## Other changes

### Staged deployment workflow

- New `prepare`, `prestate` and `continue` commands split a chain deployment into reviewable stages (#21560, #21600, #21611, #21897, #21963, #21974, #22082, #22337):
  - `prepare` pins an existing OPCM (`opcmAddress` and `superchainConfigProxy` are required in the intent), anchors each chain at the L1 `safe` block, dry-runs the deployment against an L1 fork and records the predicted addresses, L2 genesis and starting anchor root in `state.json`. It sends no transactions. `--genesis-time-offset` (`DEPLOYER_GENESIS_TIME_OFFSET`, default 21600s, minimum 3600s) sets the L2 genesis time after the anchor block. `inspect genesis` and `inspect rollup` work on a prepared state.
  - `prestate --dispute-absolute-prestate` (`DEPLOYER_DISPUTE_ABSOLUTE_PRESTATE`) records the absolute prestate for each pending `CANNON_KONA` or `SUPER_CANNON_KONA` chain.
  - `continue` refuses to run if the intent, deployer, OPCM, anchor or artifacts changed since `prepare` (rerun `prepare` instead), simulates every chain before broadcasting, checkpoints each chain as it lands and can be rerun after a failure.
  - `apply` remains the single-step path for permissioned chains. `apply` and `prepare` each refuse a state file produced by the other.

### Deploy

- `init --intent-type standard*` and the standard intent checks now target the op-contracts/v8.0.0 OPCM from the superchain registry (#22703)
- Broadcasts from `apply`, `bootstrap`, `manage` and `continue` now let the L1 node estimate gas for each transaction instead of reusing gas limits from op-deployer's own script simulation, and send transactions one at a time, stopping at the first failure. Deployments are slower but no longer fail when L1 gas costs are repriced, as with EIP-8037 in Glamsterdam. Gas estimation also no longer caps the estimate at 2^24, so the L1 node applies its own fork's limit (#21728, #22217)
- When an intent sets only `opcmAddress`, the SuperchainConfig proxy is now read from the OPCM onchain rather than looked up in the superchain registry, so deployments against an OPCM on an L1 outside the registry work (#22252)
- `bootstrap superchain` and the `apply` superchain stage no longer deploy ProtocolVersions. The `protocolVersionsProxyAddress` and `protocolVersionsImplAddress` fields are gone from the `bootstrap` outputs, and the matching fields are gone from `superchainContracts` in `state.json` (#20527)

### Genesis

- New chains now activate every hardfork up to the newest one active on OP Mainnet at genesis, read from the embedded superchain registry. In this release that is Karst; previously it was Jovian. Override the schedule with the `l2Genesis*TimeOffset` fields in the intent (#21633, #21664)
- New deploy config field `keepKarstUpgradeGas` (default `false`), written to the rollup config as `keep_karst_upgrade_gas` (#21441)
- `apply` now validates the generated L2 genesis allocs and fails with `L2 genesis allocs failed validation` if an account is unexpected or a proxy's admin and implementation slots are inconsistent (#21345)
- The generated L2 genesis no longer leaves the L2 ProxyAdmin owner account with a nonzero nonce (#21343)
- L1 dev genesis (`--deployment-target genesis`) now applies `bpo2TimeOffset`, which was previously ignored, and accepts new `l1DevGenesisParams` fields `bpo3TimeOffset`, `bpo4TimeOffset`, `bpo5TimeOffset` and `amsterdamTimeOffset` (#21920)
- L2 genesis generation for `--deployment-target genesis` now accepts contract artifacts above the EIP-170 code-size limit, such as unoptimized development builds (#21936)

### Bug fixes

- Fixed a `revision id N cannot be reverted` panic during script execution when the revision id did not start with `1`, hit on the OPCM v2 upgrade path (#21396)
- A spurious `Transaction receipt not found err="context canceled"` warning is no longer logged after a transaction confirms (#21317)

### Miscellaneous

- The artifact download progress bar is now a single line, `Downloading... NN% (x/y)`, updated once per second, and is hidden when stderr is not a terminal (#20988)

### Security

- Built with Go 1.26.5 (previously 1.24.13), picking up Go standard library security fixes (#21452, #21854)

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/compare/op-deployer/v0.7.1...op-deployer/v0.8.0

**🚢 Docker Image:**

- https://us-docker.pkg.dev/oplabs-tools-artifacts/images/op-deployer:v0.8.0

observations.name: op-batcher v1.17.2
observations.title: op-batcher v1.17.2
observations.body:
## Overview

> [!IMPORTANT]
> This is a recommended release for op-batcher operators running with `--data-availability-type=auto`, and an optional one for everyone else. It contains corrected calldata pricing on L1 chains that have activated Glamsterdam, and the removal of the server-side RPC metrics.

## Other changes

### Data availability

- With `--data-availability-type=auto`, the calldata-versus-blob cost comparison now prices calldata with the Glamsterdam gas rules once that fork is active on L1: a 15,000 gas base cost per transaction instead of 21,000, and a floor of 64 gas per calldata byte instead of 40. Previously the old model stayed in use after the fork, underestimating calldata and sometimes choosing it when blobs were cheaper. The fork is detected from the L1 block header, so no configuration is needed, and the numbers are unchanged on an L1 that has not activated it. The `Using calldata channel config` and `Using blob channel config` log lines gain an `amsterdam` field showing which rules applied (#22996)

### Metrics

- The server-side RPC metrics `op_batcher_default_rpc_server_*` (requests, durations, responses, parameter and result sizes, notifications sent) are no longer exported. Dashboards and alerts that query them need updating; the `op_batcher_default_rpc_client_*` metrics are unchanged (#23114, #23055)

### Miscellaneous

- When the batcher detects malformed transaction data it is about to submit, such as a calldata transaction carrying more than one frame, it now shuts down cleanly with a `Critical error detected, attempting batcher shut down` error log instead of exiting immediately with a `CRIT` log. Alerts matching the old `Unexpected number of frames in calldata tx` or `Unexpected blob txdata with AltDA enabled` lines need updating (#23054)

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/compare/op-batcher/v1.17.1...op-batcher/v1.17.2

**🚢 Docker Image:**

- https://us-docker.pkg.dev/oplabs-tools-artifacts/images/op-batcher:v1.17.2

observations.name: kona-node v1.7.2
observations.title: kona-node v1.7.2
observations.body:
## Overview

> [!NOTE]
>
> `kona-node` is not production-ready. Production deployments should use `op-node`.

## Other changes

### Derivation

- Singular batches whose parent hash does not match the L2 safe head are now dropped with a `parent hash does not match L2 safe head` warning, and the channel is flushed, as op-node does under Holocene. Previously kona-node replaced the parent hash of every singular batch with the safe head's hash before checking it, so such a batch, for example one built on an unsafe block that was later reorged out, was accepted and could leave kona-node with a different safe head from op-node (#23071)

### Bug fixes

- kona-node now decodes deposit transactions whose `isSystemTx` field op-geth reports as a JSON boolean, which previously failed to parse. Only deposits in pre-Regolith blocks carry the flag, so no chain in the superchain registry is affected (#22946)

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/compare/kona-node/v1.7.1...kona-node/v1.7.2

**🚢 Docker Image:**

- https://us-docker.pkg.dev/oplabs-tools-artifacts/images/kona-node:v1.7.2

observations.name: kona-host v1.8.0
observations.title: kona-host v1.8.0
observations.body:
## Overview

> [!IMPORTANT]
> This is a recommended release for all chains. It contains a derivation fix for malformed batches that only a faulty batcher could produce, stricter handling of execution errors, an EVM update, a TLS security fix, and preimage server fixes. Run it with the kona-client v1.8.0 absolute prestates.

## Other changes

### Derivation

- After Holocene, kona now checks each singular batch's parent hash against the safe head, as op-node does. Previously the check always passed, so a malformed batch from a faulty batcher could make kona derive a different chain from op-node. Fault proofs are unaffected unless the batcher misbehaves (#23071)

### Proof execution

- A block is now replaced with a deposit-only block (or dropped, before Holocene) only when its payload is actually invalid. Errors that do not prove the payload invalid, such as missing preimage or witness data, now stop the program instead of producing a deposit-only block, matching op-node (#23012)
- revm is updated from 41 to 42 with reth v2.5.2. This fixes state cleanup when a transaction fails during finalization and storage handling for destroyed accounts (#22495)

### Host

- rustls is updated to 0.23.45 for RUSTSEC-2026-0285, where a TLS 1.3 peer could send handshake messages in plaintext that should have been encrypted. It affects kona-host's TLS connections to L1, L2 and beacon RPCs (#22898)
- In `--server` mode, an I/O error on a preimage pipe no longer closes the pipe's file descriptor (#23038)
- kona-host now exits with an error when the blob provider cannot be initialised, instead of continuing without it (#22791)
- `isSystemTx` on Bedrock system deposits fetched over JSON RPC is now decoded as a boolean, so proofs over Bedrock-era blocks expect a current op-reth or op-geth endpoint (#22946)

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/compare/kona-host/v1.7.0...kona-host/v1.8.0

**🚢 Docker Image:**

- https://us-docker.pkg.dev/oplabs-tools-artifacts/images/kona-host:v1.8.0

<!--* op-revm,alloy-op-evm: exempt deposits from the gas cap in OpHandler::tx_gas (#22993) — kona already exempt; no output change-->
<!--* op-node,kona: enforce the Lagoon post-exec span batch slot rules (#22922) — Lagoon not scheduled on any chain-->
<!--* op-alloy,op-reth,kona: enforce canonical PostExec entries (#23003) — Lagoon not scheduled on any chain-->

observations.name: kona-client v1.8.0
observations.title: kona-client v1.8.0
observations.body:
## Overview

> [!IMPORTANT]
> This is a recommended release for all chains. It contains a derivation fix for malformed batches that only a faulty batcher could produce, stricter handling of execution errors in the proof program, and an EVM update, and it requires the new absolute prestates.

## Other changes

### Derivation

- After Holocene, kona now checks each singular batch's parent hash against the safe head, as op-node does. Previously the check always passed, so a malformed batch from a faulty batcher could make kona derive a different chain from op-node. Fault proofs are unaffected unless the batcher misbehaves (#23071)

### Proof execution

- A block is now replaced with a deposit-only block (or dropped, before Holocene) only when its payload is actually invalid. Errors that do not prove the payload invalid, such as missing preimage or witness data, now stop the program instead of producing a deposit-only block, matching op-node (#23012)
- revm is updated from 41 to 42 with reth v2.5.2. This fixes state cleanup when a transaction fails during finalization and storage handling for destroyed accounts (#22495)

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/compare/kona-client/v1.7.0...kona-client/v1.8.0

**🚢 Docker Image:**

- https://us-docker.pkg.dev/oplabs-tools-artifacts/images/kona-client:v1.8.0

observations.name: op-supernode v1.0.3
observations.title: op-supernode v1.0.3
observations.body:
## Overview

> [!NOTE]
> This is an optional release for op-supernode operators. It contains stricter validation of hardfork activation times in rollup configs.

## Other changes


### Configuration

- op-supernode now refuses to load a virtual node's rollup config that activates two hardforks at the same timestamp after genesis. The check applies to Jovian and every later fork, and every fork is now checked for correct activation order. Forks that activate at or before genesis may still share a timestamp. Existing chains in the superchain registry are unaffected. A custom config that schedules, say, Karst and another later fork at the same post-genesis timestamp must be corrected before upgrading (#22838)

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/compare/op-supernode/v1.0.2...op-supernode/v1.0.3

**🚢 Docker Image:**

- https://us-docker.pkg.dev/oplabs-tools-artifacts/images/op-supernode:v1.0.3
